claim: Integral membrane proteins (IMPs) comprise 20–30% of the human genome.
source: Although comprising only 20–30% of the human genome, they represent nearly two-thirds of druggable targets due to their significant impact on cellular physiology and their exposure to the cell surface.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature

claim: Integral membrane proteins represent nearly two-thirds of druggable targets.
source: Although comprising only 20–30% of the human genome, they represent nearly two-thirds of druggable targets due to their significant impact on cellular physiology and their exposure to the cell surface. This prevalence highlights the critical nature of IMPs in pharmacology (Bakheet and Doig, 2009; Fagerberg et al., 2010; Helbig et al., 2010; Santos et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to previous literature

claim: Thermal proteome profiling (TPP) is derived from the cellular thermal shift assay.
source: Derived from the cellular thermal shift assay, TPP enables the detection of ligand-induced conformational changes by assessing protein stability under heat stress (Molina et al., 2013; Savitski et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature

claim: TPP typically relies on cytosolic extracts and often overlooks pharmaceutically relevant transmembrane proteins.
source: However, TPP typically relies on cytosolic extracts and often overlooks pharmaceutically relevant transmembrane proteins (Franken et al., 2015; Mateus et al., 2020; Lambos et al., 2025).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature

claim: Detergent-based solubilization has been widely used to expand proteomics techniques to membrane proteome coverage.
source: To expand these techniques to membrane proteome coverage, detergent-based solubilization has been widely used (Huber et al., 2015; Kalxdorf et al., 2021; Reinhard et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature

claim: Even mild detergents can disrupt native protein structures or drug associations, leading to artifacts that complicate drug target identification.
source: However, even mild detergents can disrupt native protein structures or drug associations, leading to artifacts that complicate drug target identification (Berlin et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2014; Ye et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature

claim: Detergents are largely incompatible with workflows like TPP due to mass spectrometry (MS) limitations.
source: While crucial for solubilizing membrane proteins and enabling structural and functional studies (O'Malley et al., 2011; Allison et al., 2015; Beckner et al., 2020), detergents remain, as we show here, largely incompatible with workflows like TPP due to mass spectrometry (MS) limitations (Brough et al., 2024; Antony et al., 2025).
evidence: Supported by citations and reference to results shown in the manuscript

claim: The Peptidisc is characterized by its 'one-size-fits-all' property, capable of stabilizing IMPs of diverse sizes and topologies.
source: Among these, the Peptidisc has emerged as a versatile, self-assembling scaffold characterized by its 'one-size-fits-all' property, capable of stabilizing IMPs of diverse sizes and topologies (Carlson et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature

claim: Peptidisc libraries are directly compatible with downstream MS workflows.
source: This adaptability has enabled the comprehensive isolation of membrane proteomes from both bacterial and mammalian sources, yielding the so-called Peptidisc libraries that are directly compatible with downstream MS workflows (Antony et al., 2024; Carlson et al., 2019; Zhao et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature

claim: Peptidisc libraries capture and stabilize IMPs in their functional states while preserving their interactomes and lipid allosteric modulators.
source: In addition to MS compatibility, these libraries also capture and stabilize IMPs in their functional states while preserving their interactomes and lipid allosteric modulators, thus enabling a more comprehensive analysis of membrane protein dynamics and ligand interactions (Angiulli et al., 2020; Carlson et al., 2019; Jandu et al., 2024; Urner et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature

claim: Vanadate is a potent inhibitor of the ABC transporter family.

evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature
